paragraphs: On Monday morning, Lily and Tom sat on a long seat next to the window. It was raining, and the glass was wet. Lily had her school bag on her knees, and Tom held a wet umbrella. The driver stopped at a railway gate, and the red lights came on. Many cars waited in front of them.

"Why do we stop?" asked Lily. "A train is coming," said Tom. "If the gate is down, everything waits." "There is a lot of traffic today," said Lily. "Yes, because of the rain," said Tom. "Look, a man on a bicycle is going past us!" "He is faster than we are," said Lily, and she laughed.

A taxi stopped next to the window. A woman inside looked at her phone. "How long is our journey to school?" asked Lily. "It is twenty minutes," said Tom, "but today it is longer." "It is ten past eight now, and we are not late." "Is our school far from the railway?" asked Lily. "No, it is near," said Tom. "We are there soon after the train goes."

Lily took a small paper and a pencil from her bag. She drew a round silver spaceship with a window. Tom looked at the picture and nodded. "My spaceship has no traffic and no railway," she said. "The journey to school takes one minute." "And no rain?" asked Tom. "No rain," said Lily. "But there is a window, so I can see the stars."

Then the train went past with a loud sound. The gate went up, and the cars began to move. "Our stop is next," said Tom. He pushed the red bell above the window. "Next stop, the school," said the driver. Lily put the spaceship in her bag, and she smiled. "Perhaps I can send it to Leo for a cartoon," she said.
